$comment: D-TARGET-ENCODING-WIDTH-GUARD (LD-5): the runtime witness for NEGATING a `long double` and for CONVERTING one to and from every narrower scalar, on every long-double axis. ✔MEASURED BEFORE THE CHANGE, through the shipped CLI at b1f31420 with one tiny program per operation compiled ALONE so no refusal could mask another, SEVEN of the operations below REFUSED with `L_UnsupportedLoweringForOpcode` naming this anchor: `-ld` (MIR FNeg, BOTH axes), `(unsigned)ld` (MIR FPToUI (source), BOTH), `(double)ld` and `(float)ld` (MIR FPTrunc (source), BOTH), `(long double)someFloat` (MIR FPExt (result), BOTH), `(long double)someDouble` (MIR FPExt (result), x87 only — arm64 already had the `from_f64` row), and `(long long)ld` (MIR FPToSI (source), arm64; on x87 it said `MIR opcode '<deferred>'` instead). The baseline was FAIL LOUD with no binary, never a wrong answer; the f64 axis (pe64 x86_64, Apple arm64), where `long double` IS `double`, already ran every arm, which is what makes one program meaningful on all three. TWO REALIZATIONS, dispatched on TypeKind alone: on the x87-80 axis an INLINE memory sequence built from six new byte-verified opcode rows (`fchs` D9 E0; `fld_m32` D9 /0; `fld_m64` DD /0; `fstp_m32` D9 /3; `fstp_m64` DD /3; `fisttp_m64` DD /1) — the x87 stack has ONE working format and no register-to-register conversion, so every format change happens in the memory operand; on the ieee128 axis a CALL to one of six new config'd libgcc helpers (`__negtf2`, `__fixunstfsi`, `__fixtfdi`, `__trunctfdf2`, `__trunctfsf2`, `__extendsftf2`), gated on the PRESENCE of the row and never on target identity. ★★ WHAT EACH ARM MEASURES, because a long-double program that compiles and returns 42 proves NO FAULT and nothing about whether the conversion was CORRECT — none of these operations faults when it is wrong, each returns a plausible number: arms 1-3 that the three ULPS the file discovers at runtime (of `float`, `double` and `long double`, each found by halving in that type's own arithmetic, since DSS ships no <float.h>) are non-zero, without which every width arm below would be vacuously true; arms 4-5 NEGATE DIRECTION (a no-op or an absolute value fails) and its agreement with `0 - x` on a non-zero value; arm 6 NEGATE AT FULL WIDTH — negate a value whose LAST mantissa bit is significant and add it back, so a negate that round-tripped through anything narrower leaves a residue, with a second half that stops the arm passing vacuously; arm 7 `(unsigned)` truncating TOWARD ZERO; arm 8 THE RANGE ARM — `(unsigned)3000000000.0L` is above 2^31, so a lowering that stored through the x87 32-bit truncating form would write the 0x80000000 integer-indefinite here with no fault at all; arm 9 `(long long)` truncating toward zero on the NEGATIVE side (-7.9 → -7, the direction a floor-based lowering gets wrong only for negatives); arm 10 `(long long)` WIDTH — 2^53 is built by doubling and 2^53+1 requested back, with the expected answer derived SELF-CALIBRATINGLY from the type's own comparison so the arm is exact on a 53-, 64- or 113-bit mantissa while still missing under any 32-bit or float-mediated conversion; arms 11-13 the NARROWINGS, with 12 and 13 placing the value THREE QUARTERS of the way between two representable neighbours so round-to-nearest and truncation give DIFFERENT answers (a halfway-point arm passes under both), and 13 additionally separating `fstp m32` from `fstp m64`, which differ in one opcode byte; arm 14 cross-checking that `(double)ld` loses exactly what it should, the predicate derived from the two discovered ulps rather than assumed; arms 15-16 the WIDENINGS with the LOW BIT INTACT — widen 1+ulp(1.0f) and 1+ulp(1.0) and recover that ulp by subtraction in long-double arithmetic, which is full width by construction, so a widen that read the wrong four bytes (`fld m32` on an 8-byte slot) misses; arms 17-19 exactness and both round trips. ⓘ ARM 20 IS THE x87 STACK-BALANCE ARM AND NO STRAIGHT-LINE ARM REPLACES IT: every sequence this cycle adds pushes onto the eight-deep x87 register stack and pops again, so leaking one entry overflows it by the eighth iteration and every later result is an indefinite NaN; arm 20 runs all six new sequences — negate twice, both narrowings, both widenings, both integer conversions — forty times round a loop and checks the value on every iteration, with arms 21-23 checking the accumulated sums afterwards. ⓘ THE SIGN OF ZERO IS THE ONE CORNER NOT ARMED, and that is stated rather than faked: C compares +0.0 and -0.0 EQUAL, and distinguishing them needs either <math.h>'s signbit (DSS ships no headers) or a byte view of an object whose padding the x87 axis leaves indeterminate — an arm there would pass either way. ANTI-FOLD: every operand and every loop bound is read from a MUTABLE GLOBAL, so release cannot constant-fold a conversion away and leave the lowering untested; the release arm measures the same conversions through Mem2Reg-promoted values (the long-double locals become real phis across the loops' back edges) rather than through memory traffic. ✔REFERENCE ORACLE, each probed SEPARATELY and every one returning 42: WSL gcc 13.3.0 (-O0/-O2), WSL clang 18.1.3 (-O0/-O2), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 native (-O0/-O2), aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 under qemu-aarch64 (-O0/-O2), and MSVC 19.51.36252 at /std:c17 /O2 — the last one BUILT AND RAN to 42, so it is a positive vote on the f64 axis and not merely a front-end abstention. Lowering is pinned in the unit suite by the MirToLir F80Neg*/F80Convert*/F128Convert* tests in tests/lir/test_mir_to_lir.cpp, including the config-row-absence fail-loud arm and the AAPCS64 width-32 capture arm. ── P66 ADDED ARMS 24-27, `(unsigned long long)ld` — the LAST long-double conversion and the only one whose realization has TWO arms and a select between them. ✔MEASURED BEFORE THE CHANGE, through the shipped CLI at de1e83ef with one program per operation compiled ALONE: it REFUSED with `MIR FPToUI (source)` naming this anchor on BOTH axes, the last operation in the file that did. TWO REALIZATIONS AND THEY DO NOT SHARE AN ALGEBRA — x87-80 gets an INLINE branchless truncate-both-and-select built from opcode rows that were ALREADY declared (no new row was needed: `fld_m80`, `fld_m64`, `fsubp`, `fisttp_m64`, then `shr_a`/`and`/`or`), which is byte-for-byte the algebra x86_64.target.json already declares for `fp_to_ui` from an F64 source; ieee128 gets ONE config'd call to `__fixunstfdi`. ⚠⚠ LIFTING ONE OVER BOTH WOULD BE A SILENT MISCOMPILE: the x87 arm keys on FISTTP writing the integer INDEFINITE (0x8000000000000000) out of range, while libgcc's `__fixtfdi` SATURATES to 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF — ✔MEASURED under qemu-aarch64 — so the range mask would be ZERO on that axis and every value above 2^63 would come back wrong. ★ WHY ARM 25 USES THREE VALUES AND NOT ONE: a lowering that shipped only the direct truncation returns the indefinite above 2^63, and the indefinite IS 2^63, so a witness that stopped at the boundary would pass; 1.5*2^63 and 2^64-2048 are the values that discriminate, and the second also catches a WRONG BIAS. All four values (2^62, 2^63, 1.5*2^63, 2^64-2048) are exact in binary64, x87-80 and binary128 alike — in [2^63, 2^64) a binary64's ulp is 2048 — so one program reads the same on every axis with nothing calibrated, and each check builds its long double by DOUBLING and its expected integer by SHIFTING so neither side comes from the conversion under test. Arm 24 is the below-2^63 CONTROL; arm 26 is truncation toward zero including `(unsigned long long)(-0.5L)`, the one NEGATIVE case C defines (the integral part is zero, which IS representable) — ✔MEASURED that WSL gcc 13.3.0, WSL clang 18.1.3 and aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 all answer 7 and 0 there; arm 27 is a SECOND stack-balance loop, separate from arm 20 because this is the only operation in the file that pushes the x87 stack TWICE for one C operation (the source, then the bias on top of it), so it is the one most able to leak a pop. ✔REFERENCE ORACLE re-run on the EXTENDED file, each probed SEPARATELY and every one returning 42: WSL gcc 13.3.0 (-O0/-O2), WSL clang 18.1.3 (-O0/-O2), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 native (-O0/-O2), aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 under qemu-aarch64 (-O0/-O2), and MSVC 19.51 at /std:c17 /O2 which BUILT AND RAN it to 42. Lowering is pinned by the MirToLir F80UnsignedSixtyFourBit* arms (order, direction and the bias CONSTANT) plus the F128 `__fixunstfdi` mapping arm and its config-row-absence fail-loud sibling. ── P66 ALSO ADDED ARMS 28-32 (LD-7), `long double ld = anInt;` — THE LAST DIRECTION of this surface and the only operation family whose FOUR spellings reach FOUR different realizations. ✔MEASURED BEFORE THE CHANGE through the shipped CLI at de1e83ef, one program per operation compiled ALONE: all four spellings REFUSED rc 1 on BOTH long-double axes with `MIR SIToFP`/`MIR UIToFP` — "integer→float result TypeKind ordinal 14/15 is not lowerable … only an F64 (double) destination has an int→float encoding this cycle" — while every one of them already compiled on the f64 axis, which is what makes one program meaningful on all three. ✔ALL FOUR REFERENCES compile AND RUN it correctly, each probed separately over -3, 4294967295u, -1234567890123456789LL and 18446744073709551615ULL. TWO REALIZATIONS, dispatched on the result TypeKind alone and sharing NO algebra: on x87-80 an INLINE sequence built from TWO new byte-verified opcode rows (`fild_m32` DB /0, `fild_m64` DF /5) — `fild m32` for a signed 32-bit source, a register ZEXT then `fild m64` for an unsigned one, `fild m64` for a signed 64-bit one, and for `unsigned long long` the straight-line exact split `2*(u>>1) + (u&1)`, which is EXACT rather than merely correctly rounded because x87-80 carries a 64-bit significand (gcc 13.3.0 BRANCHES here and clang 18.1.3 indexes a two-entry constant table; DSS needs neither); on ieee128 FOUR new config'd `wideFloatSoftcalls[]` rows (`__floatsitf`, `__floatunsitf`, `__floatditf`, `__floatunditf`, all `nm -D`-verified DEFINED text exports of libgcc_s.so.1), gated on the PRESENCE of the row and never on target identity — x86_64 declares F128 with no table and still walls loud, which is pinned. ⚠ THE FAILURE MODE OF EVERY ARM HERE IS A SIGN AND IT IS SILENT: both `fild` forms read their bytes SIGNED, so an `unsigned` at or above 2^31 and an `unsigned long long` at or above 2^63 come back NEGATIVE from a lowering that skipped the widening or the split. Arm 28 asks for INT_MIN (an unsigned-form lowering answers +2^31); arm 29 for 2^31 and 2^32-1; arm 30 for -1 as a `long long` and for 2^53+1 self-calibrated exactly as arm 10 does in the opposite direction; arm 31 for 2^63, 1.5*2^63 and 2^64-2048 — all three exact in binary64, x87-80 and binary128 alike, so nothing is calibrated — plus 2^63+1 and 2^64-1 under a runtime test of whether the axis has 64 significand bits, which is what catches a low-bit mask other than 1. ★ UNLIKE ARM 25, THE BOUNDARY ITSELF DISCRIMINATES HERE: a signed read of 2^63 is -2^63, not 2^63. Arm 32 is the stack-balance loop for all four, and the deepest in the file — the unsigned-64 conversion pushes the x87 stack THREE times for one C operation — with its source ALTERNATING between two values so the conversion cannot be hoisted out of the loop. ⚠⚠ ARMS 28-32 BRIEFLY LIVED IN A FUNCTION OF THEIR OWN AND ARE BACK INSIDE `main` (P66, lane `ra`), which is what closes [[D-AS-REGALLOC-SCRATCH-POOL-EXHAUSTED-BY-A-LARGE-FUNCTION-IN-RELEASE]]. ✔MEASURED by lane `ld` with the arms written inside `main`, the same source REFUSED at `pe64-x86_64-windows-exec --config=release` with `L_VirtualRegInPostRegalloc … exhausted the per-class scratch pool` while building and running at `--config=debug`, and while the pre-P66 file built and ran at BOTH; moving them out was recorded as a WORKAROUND IN A TEST FIXTURE, never a design choice. ★★ IT WAS NEVER A FUNCTION-SIZE LIMIT AND THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE SAID IT WAS: ✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI on the SAME target and config, probes spilling 107 and 119 vregs compiled CLEAN while this file at 50 refused. The allocator reserves, per register class, as many spill-reload scratch registers as the function's peak SINGLE-INSTRUCTION reload demand, and it could draw them only from that class's NON-ARGUMENT CALLER-SAVED registers — of which `ms_x64` declares exactly TWO in the FPR class (xmm4, xmm5) against a demand of THREE, so the reservation came up one short and the shortfall stayed invisible until a function's pressure happened to assign every other FPR. ✔The refusal named class `fpr` at opcode `fadd`, pool 2, reserved 2 of 3. The shortfall now comes out of the class's CALLEE-saved registers — already legitimate scratch (the rewriter's pool harvests any unassigned allocatable register) and already saved, because the callee-save scan reads the POST-REWRITE instruction stream; ✔MEASURED in the emitted pe64 release binary, `main`'s prologue saves xmm15 and the reloads stage through it. ⓘ THIS FILE IS THEREFORE A CLI-LEVEL WITNESS AT A REAL THRESHOLD, but the property that cannot go vacuous is pinned in the unit suite by `LirRegAlloc.ReloadScratchReservationMeetsItsDemandOnEveryShippedConvention`, which asserts reserved >= demanded for every shipped convention and names no function size. ✔RUN, not merely compiled: exit 42 on `elf64-x86_64-linux-exec` (native WSL — the x87-80 axis and every new inline sequence), `elf64-aarch64-linux-exec` (qemu-aarch64 — the ieee128 axis and all four helpers) and `pe64-x86_64-windows-exec` (native Windows — the f64 axis), each x debug AND release, RE-RUN on the re-inlined file; `macho64-arm64-darwin-exec` and `macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec` BUILD rc 0 x debug and release but were NOT executed, because this host has no darwin runner and the leg was not taken. ✔REFERENCE ORACLE re-run on the EXTENDED file, each probed SEPARATELY and every one returning 42: WSL gcc 13.3.0 (-O0/-O2), WSL clang 18.1.3 (-O0/-O2), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 native (-O0/-O2), aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 under qemu-aarch64 (-O0/-O2), and MSVC 19.51.36231 at /std:c17 /O2 which BUILT AND RAN it. Lowering is pinned by the MirToLir IntToF80*/UInt64ToF80*/IntToF128* arms and the sub-native source wall. ── P66 ALSO ADDED ARMS 33-34 (LD-7), `!someLongDouble` AND THE LONG-DOUBLE `_Complex` ZERO, which are ONE defect through two doors: C 6.5.3.3p5 makes `!E` exactly `(0 == E)` for any scalar, so `!ld` needs a long-double ZERO to compare against, and a register machine has no float-immediate form — the zero must be promoted to an anonymous rodata global and LOADED. `elementFloatConst` in hir_to_mir.cpp gated that promotion on F64/F32 ONLY, so on a wide long-double axis the zero fell through to a bare MIR `Const` and dead-ended at MIR→LIR with `MIR Const %N is a float (FPR-class) literal`, a diagnostic naming THIS anchor. The real→complex construct's imaginary 0.0 comes from the SAME helper, so `long double _Complex z = 2.0L;` and `!z` refused for the same reason; widening that ONE gate to admit F80/F128 fixes all three, and the promotion itself needed nothing new (lowerMirGlobalsToDataItems already widens a double-armed literal to the 80-/128-bit data item an F80/F128 global needs, which is how a source `long double g = 3.25L;` has worked since LD-1). ⚠⚠ A CLOSED ROW CLAIMS THIS ALREADY WORKED: [[D-CSUBSET-LOGICAL-NOT-ON-A-FLOAT-MINTS-A-BARE-FLOAT-CONST]] (P41) states in its trigger that "`!f`, `!d` and `!ld` compile" — ✔MEASURED on `x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec`, THE ONE AXIS WHERE `long double` IS `double`, so `!ld` there is `!d` under another spelling; that row's own FIX note correctly says F16/F80/F128 kept falling through, so its headline and its body disagreed and the headline was the false half. ✔MEASURED at de1e83ef through the shipped CLI that `!ld` and `!!ld` refused rc 1 on BOTH `elf64-x86_64-linux-exec` (F80) and `elf64-aarch64-linux-exec` (F128) while compiling on pe64, and so did `long double _Complex z = 2.0L;` and `!z`. Arm 34's values are built so that reading only ONE component changes the answer — (0,7) is truthy only if the imaginary part is read, and it must not compare equal to (5,0) — the same construction c99_complex_truth uses for its F64/F32 elements; it lives HERE rather than there because what it measures is the long-double WIDTH, not complex comparison semantics. ✔All four references compile and RUN both arms, and the whole file still returns 42 from every reference configuration listed above. Lowering is pinned by `MirLoweringC.LogicalNotOnALongDoubleAlsoComparesAgainstAPromotedZero`, which names the AXIS in its fixture (LongDoubleFormat::X87_80 and ::Ieee128) and asserts the operand's TypeKind really is F80/F128 before asserting the zero is a Load — the premise the P41 arm never had. ── P66 ALSO ADDED ARM 34 (LD-7), THE SUB-NATIVE INTEGER RESULTS — `(char)ld`, `(signed char)ld`, `(short)ld`, `(unsigned char)ld`, `(unsigned short)ld` — WHICH IS THE LAST REFUSAL ON THIS SURFACE AND THE ONE WHOSE CAUSE THIS ROW GOT WRONG. ✔MEASURED at de1e83ef, one program per operation: the three signed spellings refused with `MIR opcode '<deferred>'` and the two unsigned ones with `MIR FPToUI (source)`, on BOTH long-double axes, while all five compiled on the f64 axis. ⚠⚠ THE ROW'S CLOSING-WORK CELL DELEGATED THEM TO [[D-CSUBSET-SUBNATIVE-ALU-FORMS]] AND THAT DELEGATION IS REFUTED: ✔MEASURED on the SAME target that `(unsigned char)someDouble`, `(short)someDouble`, `(signed char)someDouble`, `(unsigned char)someFloat` and `(unsigned char)someInt` ALL compiled rc 0 the whole time, so the sub-native integer FORM was never what was missing. What was missing was one WORD in THREE places: the long-double FPToSI/FPToUI dispatches and `lowerF80ToInt` each asked `memAccessWidthFlags` for the RESULT's width — a question about how many BYTES an object of that type OCCUPIES, answering 8 for `unsigned char` and 16 for `short`, widths no arm has — where a conversion RESULT is a register-resident VALUE and a sub-native integer lives PROMOTED in a 32-bit register with its low bits significant (C 6.3.1.1), the narrowing realizing at the width-exact STORE. `registerOpWidthFlags` is that question, and the softcall's own result CAPTURE was already asking it, so the two ends of one call disagreed. All THREE sites moved together ([[feedback-a-partial-fix-reads-as-a-complete-one]]). ★ ONLY IN-RANGE VALUES ARE ASKED FOR and that is not timidity: C 6.3.1.4 makes an out-of-range float→integer conversion UNDEFINED, so an out-of-range arm would measure nothing the references must agree on. The discriminating values are the ones ABOVE the signed sub-native range and inside the unsigned one — 200 for `unsigned char`, 60000 for `unsigned short` — which a realization narrowing to a SIGNED 8 or 16 bits answers with -56 and -5536; plain `char` is only asked for values that fit BOTH readings, since its signedness is per-platform (✔signed on x86_64-linux, unsigned on aarch64-linux, both measured through the CLI, which is why `(long double)aChar` fires SIToFP on one target and UIToFP on the other). Lowering is pinned by `MirToLir.LongDoubleToSubNativeIntegerUsesTheRegisterWidthNotTheMemoryOne`, which asserts each sub-native result takes the SAME realization as its 32-bit sibling BY EQUALITY OF SHAPE rather than by restating the shape, and that a sub-native F128 result reaches the 32-bit helper (`__fixtfsi`/`__fixunstfsi`) rather than a narrower one. exit = 42; each arm returns its own number so a failure names itself.
